newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 13.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
* Gillette Co agreed to buy Duracell International Inc for $7 billion in stock.

* The Federal Trade Commission's approval of the merger of Time Warner Inc and Turner Broadcasting System Inc backed away from the hard line on media mergers that many thought was underway at the agency.
* Federal prosecutors have told Archer Daniels Midland Co and two of its senior executives that indictments on charges of an international price-fixing conspiracy could come as early as Tuesday.
* Stock prices rose after the producer price index showed little sign of inflation amid strong economic growth and corporate profits.
* Tudor Investment Corp, without admitting or denying any charges, agreed to pay $800,000 in fines to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to settle allegations of market manipulation.
* Apple Computer Inc and Hewlett-Packard Co are in talks aimed at the joint development of ink-jet printers.
* The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved a model of small defibrillators made by Heartstream Inc.
